column2: Configure redundant destinations and scopes; validate lease continuity, renewal, and rebinding.
Replicate the scope (with non-overlapping ranges) on another destination server to keep granting new leases after a failure.
On at least one destination server, create a pool whose network contains the giaddr; separate pools must use non-overlapping ranges.
{0}: VNI {1} uses static flooding/learning; RT limits control-plane import only.
Use peerPolicy evpn to require imported IMET members in the data plane; also validate isolation by VNI/VRF/ACL.
Check import/export and the flooding policy. An empty RIB does not prove isolation in static mode.
Use a /32 loopback and return routes over independent operational paths.
Review guest access to sensitive zones. A zone-wide permit may include MES and PLC; validate the destinations with negative scenarios.
{0}: application inspection uses IPv4 only; transit zones cover IPv4/IPv6.
Configure equivalent IPv6 ACLs/zones or reject the use case that depends on IPv6 application inspection.
{0}: Hello/Dead {1}/{2} s vs {3}/{4} s; the adjacency does not form.
{0}: OSPF areas {1}/{2} on the same segment; the adjacency does not form.
Place both interfaces in the same area.
{0}: network types {1}/{2}; the adjacency may form, but SPF discards the link.
Use the same ip ospf network on both ends.
{0}: IP MTU {1}/{2} on the OSPF segment; the adjacency gets stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE.
Match the MTU of the interfaces on the segment.
{0}: network {1} has no exact route in the routing table; the prefix is not advertised.
BGP only advertises a network with an identical route (connected, static, or IGP). Create the exact route or adjust the network mask.
{0}: NAT rules without an {1} interface; nothing is translated.
Mark the LAN interface with ip nat inside and the outgoing interface with ip nat outside.
{0} and {1} translate the same inside network without shared NAT state; replies returning through the other router are dropped.
Ensure traffic exits and returns through the same router (routes/HSRP priority), or configure an HA pair with state replication.
{0} L3 switch(es) forward IP; stateful transit firewalling requires a router in the current model.
Use ACLs on the switch or a dedicated firewall profile for stateful inspection.
The addresses share the Ethernet domain inferred from the configured links/VLANs/VNIs; resolve the conflict.
Pools {0}/{1}: overlapping ranges in the same domain.
Use distinct ranges or implement authoritative lease replication before enabling both servers.
Link {0}: reference to a nonexistent interface.
Reconnect the link to valid interfaces.
Match the native VLANs on both ends.
{0}: one end is trunk and the other is access; only the native/access VLAN passes.
Configure switchport mode trunk on both ends (uplink) or access on both (user port).
{0}: access ports in VLANs {1}/{2} merge two broadcast domains.
Use the same VLAN on both ends or a trunk; IOS CDP would report a native VLAN mismatch.
{0}: VLANs allowed on only one end — {1}: {2}; {3}: {4}.
These VLANs are not carried over the trunk; align switchport trunk allowed vlan if they are needed.
Create the VLAN (vlan N); in IOS, an access port in a nonexistent VLAN is inactive.
{0}: duplex {1}/{2}; expect late collisions and loss under load.
Use the same duplex setting (or autonegotiation) on both ends.
{0}: IP MTU {1}/{2}; OSPF gets stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE and large packets are dropped.
Match the MTU (or ip mtu) on both ends.
Check power, interface, media, and distance.
Check dependents, state/data, and the redundancy strategy; duplicating the device is not enough.
Physical RF positions not configured on all radios.
Configure all pairs in meters; incomplete pairs still use the diagram coordinates.
{0} additional findings exceeded the review limit.
Split the topology or fix the existing findings before completing the review.
